depth_justification: The copilot does anchor to this app's actual choices (chat-surfaced vs ToS disclaimer, Mistral-7B fine-tuned on synthetic GPT-4 CBT dialogues, mood-logging engagement loop, bundled 14-page-PDF consent, anxiety as a vulnerable group) and cites named provisions (EU AI Act Art. 50, Annex III, Art. 27, GDPR Art. 9(2)(a)). But it is heavily templated and partly inaccurate: the high-risk/conformity-assessment/FRIA block is recycled near-verbatim across four turns, it repeatedly invokes a non-existent 'Swiss AI Act', and it uses HERA dimension IDs ([P2.D3], [P4.D12], [P4.D8]) that don't match the gold-standard set, with a final report that drifts further from what was discussed.
actionability_justification: There are a few implementable items (add an explicit 'You are chatting with an AI assistant' notice in the chat UI, split out plain-language granular opt-in consent for health-data processing, add a UI label distinguishing clinically-reviewed vs AI-generated CBT content, give users control over engagement frequency). But the bulk is circular and directional ('conduct a conformity assessment', 'reassess your classification', 'apply enhanced data protection measures') without telling the developer how to actually run the SaMD/risk-tier determination, and the FRIA recommendation under Art. 27 is misapplied to a private startup with only a one-time caveat.
salient_examples: add a clear notice in the chat interface that explicitly states "You are chatting with an AI assistant"
you must ensure compliance with both the EU AI Act and the Swiss AI Act, which may have similar transparency requirements
You must conduct a conformity assessment under the EU AI Act, including a Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment (FRIA) if your app is used in a public service or by a public body
You must implement separate, plain-language consent mechanisms specifically for processing sensitive health content in chats and mood logs
